land.text: the Pyrenean valleys of Pallars, Toulousain land after Bernard II of Toulouse was assassinated in 872

predecessors.note: The page: 'In 872, a crisis enveloped Toulouse when the incumbent count, Bernard II, was assassinated'; Raymond I 'seized authority for himself in Pallars and Ribagorza'. Cliopatria's West Franks row (850-989) is the nominal overlord; county-of-ribagorza gives the same predecessor.

land.text: Pallars Jussà: the Tremp and Pobla de Segur side

successors.note: 'In 1011, Sunyer of Pallars died and by his testament his county was divided between his sons ... Raymond III, receiving Pallars Jussà' (County of Pallars Jussà page).

land.text: Pallars Sobirà: Sort and the upper valleys

successors.note: William II received Pallars Sobirà in the same division of 1011.

capitals.name: Sort
capitals.note: The page 'names Sort as the chief city, without a date'; no page opened names a capital for the county before the division. The Jussà page puts the capital of Pallars Jussà at Segur (La Pobla de Segur) after 1011 and says that 'by the year 1000, the economic and social centre of Pallars was located in the Pobla de Segur and Tremp'. Coordinates are the researcher's.

rulers.name: Raymond I
rulers.note: 'the first independent count of Pallars and Ribagorza from 872 until his death' (Raymond I page); the County page lists 872-920. He lost most of Ribagorza to Huesca in 907.

rulers.name: Lope I
rulers.note: Joint rule with Isarn: Pallars passed to Raymond I's two youngest sons (County page list: Lope I 920-947).

rulers.name: Isarn
rulers.note: Joint rule with Lope I (County page list: Isarn 920-948).

rulers.name: Raymond II
rulers.note: Joint rule with his brothers Borrell I and Sunyer I (County page list: 948-992).

rulers.name: Sunyer I
rulers.note: 'who had outlived his brothers and nephews, and died in 1011' (County page); his sons divided the county.

rulers.name: Ermengol I
rulers.note: Listed on the County page as 992-1010 beside Sunyer I; the page text opened does not say how he was related. Not otherwise confirmed.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 872-874: Cliopatria starts in 875 but the Raymond I page dates the first independent count to 872 ('the first independent count of Pallars and Ribagorza from 872 until his death'). The 875 outline (18 H3 cells, 4,850 km2) is applied back; the pages give names (Pallars, Sort, Tremp), not an extent.

875-883, 4,850 km2, 18 H3 cells (Tremp, Sort, the upper valleys and, by the grid test, the Aran valley and Àger). The page has no infobox and no area; the sum of Cliopatria's later Jussà (1,596 km2) and Sobirà (3,039 km2) shapes is 4,635 km2, ratio 0.96. Raymond I held Ribagorza as well until 907 (Raymond I page), which Cliopatria draws as its own County of Ribagorza row.

990-1009, 4,779 km2: the same 18 cells; no page explains the small change in the outline.

keyframe_review.note: 1010-1014, 4,779 km2: the same 18 cells. The county ended in 1011 ('In 1011, Sunyer of Pallars died and by his testament his county was divided between his sons'), so the shape holds for 1010-1011; from 1011 the land is Pallars Jussà and Pallars Sobirà, whose Cliopatria shapes start only in 1040.

region.text: Pallars, the Pyrenean valleys round Sort and Tremp

ledger.note: 872: Raymond I makes himself count of Pallars and Ribagorza. 'in the aftermath of the assassination of Bernard II of Toulouse by partisans of Bernard Plantapilosa (872)' he seized authority for himself in Pallars and Ribagorza; 'the first independent count of Pallars and Ribagorza from 872 until his death'. The County page: 'In 872, a crisis enveloped Toulouse when the incumbent count, Bernard II, was assassinated.' The pages give the pagi, not an outline; Ribagorza is drawn by county-of-ribagorza.

region.text: Pallars Jussà: the Tremp and Pobla de Segur side

ledger.note: 1011: Sunyer dies and the county is divided; Raymond III takes Pallars Jussà. 'In 1011, Sunyer of Pallars died and by his testament his county was divided between his sons ... the eldest, Raymond III, receiving Pallars Jussà'.

region.text: Pallars Sobirà: Sort and the upper valleys

ledger.note: 1011: William II takes Pallars Sobirà in the same division ('the younger, William II, receiving Pallars Sobirà'). The County page: 'Sunyer's two sons divided their inheritance, with Raymond III ruling in Pallars Jussà and William II in Pallars Sobirà.'
1011: the undivided county of Pallars ends. Sunyer 'who had outlived his brothers and nephews, and died in 1011'; his two sons divided the inheritance (the page gives no separate date for the split).

wars.name: Muhammad al-Tawil's conquest of Ribagorza (907)
wars.outcome: Raymond I lost much of Ribagorza, including Roda and Montpedrós, to Muhammad al-Tawil of Huesca in 907 and thereafter ruled mainly Pallars.
wars.note: No border of Cliopatria's County of Pallars row moves: Ribagorza is a separate Cliopatria row (see county-of-ribagorza, which records the 907 loss). The County page repeats it: 'He lost much of Ribagorza to Huesca in 907 and thereafter ruled mainly just Pallars'. The Muslim alliances with Huesca and Zaragoza and the 'Reconquista' policy of the later counts are undated on the page.

certainty.note: A Pyrenean valley county: the pages name valleys and towns, never a boundary line; the outline is Cliopatria's stand-in throughout.

sources.title: County of Pallars
sources.note: No infobox. Origin in 872, the 907 loss of Ribagorza, 920 division, count list, Sunyer's death and the division of 1011, Sort as chief city.

sources.title: Raymond I of Pallars and Ribagorza
sources.note: 872 seizure of power, first independent count, 907 loss of Ribagorza to Muhammad al-Tawil of Huesca; no death year (fl. 884-920), no seat.

sources.title: County of Pallars Jussà

notes:
Written by the Phase B agent eu-12-b on 2026-10-25 from four pages (budget 5), one of them thin. WebFetch returns paraphrase for part of each page; fragments in quotes are the tool's.
ROW. Cliopatria's County of Pallars (875-1014) is five shapes of the same 18 H3 cells (Tremp, Sort, Pallars Sobirà valleys, Aran, Àger); the 1040 shapes of Pallars Jussà (7 cells) and Pallars Sobirà (12 cells) cover the same land plus one cell. Nothing moves between the five shapes, so the ledger has no gain or loss: the county is founded in 872 (three years before the row) and divided in 1011 (three years before the row ends); the other dossiers (county-of-pallars-jussa, county-of-pallars-sobira) have the matching 1011 'found' events and apply their 1040 shapes back to 1011, so the cells 1011-1014 are drawn by them as well as by the 1010 shape here: the renderer should end this state in 1011 (the successors found in 1011 in the same year).
NOT DRAWN OR UNDATED. Raymond I's lands in Ribagorza (872-907) belong to county-of-ribagorza; the 920 division (Pallars to Isarn and Lope I, Ribagorza to Miró and Bernard Unifred) is on the Raymond I and County pages but moves no cell of this state. The page gives no seat before the division (Sort is the 'chief city', undated). The Muslim alliances and the Reconquista policy of the 10th-century counts are undated. The ruler list is the County page's, with joint rulers overlapping; the entry for Ermengol I (992-1010) is as the page lists it and unexplained by the text opened.
AREA. No page gives an area. The Cliopatria figure (4,850 km2) is within 4 percent of the sum of the two successor shapes.
Gazetteer names needed: none (the regions used are Cliopatria shapes).
